deed: קזימיר פונק טבע את המושג ויטמין וזיהה שמחלות נגרמות ממחסור
title: Casimir Funk coined the word “vitamin” and showed that diseases are caused by deficiencies in food

trailer.text: Casimir Funk (1884–1967) was a Polish-American biochemist whom the American Nutrition Association inducted into the Nutrition Hall of Fame.

According to a historical article in PMC, Casimir Funk was born in Warsaw, the son of a Polish physician, and the upheaval of two World Wars, combined with his Polish Jewish ancestry, led to a career that spanned the United States and five European countries.
According to Funk, for years deficiency diseases were considered either intoxications by food or infectious diseases.
According to Live Science, in 1912 Funk discovered that diseases such as scurvy and rickets are caused by a lack of specific components of food.
According to the PMC article, the work led to the discovery of 13 vitamins within 35 years.

stations.title: Before: a disease without an explanation

paragraphs.text: According to Funk, for years deficiency diseases were considered either intoxications by food or infectious diseases.
He wrote that many believed that beriberi, which broke out like an epidemic, is caused by infection.
According to Funk, beriberi occurs in countries such as Japan, Malaya, the Philippines and Indochina, where rice is a staple food.
According to Encyclopedia.com, at the time of Funk's study it was not known that beriberi is caused by a lack of B1, only that it appeared in areas where polished rice was eaten.
According to the University of Bristol, on a nine-month voyage to Hawaii, 169 of 376 Japanese cadets contracted beriberi, and 25 of them died.
According to the same source, in Japan's war against Russia in 1904–1905, more than 200,000 soldiers contracted beriberi, and 27,000 died.
Funk reported that Takaki nearly succeeded in eradicating the disease from the Japanese navy when he added meat to the diet.
According to MDedge, beriberi disappeared from the Japanese navy within six years of this change.
Funk noted that Eijkman and Vorderman reached their conclusion after an investigation in 101 jails in Java in 1895–1896.
According to Funk, Eijkman determined that fowls that ate polished rice developed a disease he called polyneuritis gallinarum.
According to the University of Utah, Eijkman's fowls recovered when they were given unpolished rice, and the disease disappeared.
According to Time, in Funk's own experiment, pigeons that were given rice with its husk thrived, and those that were not given it suffered from polyneuritis.
According to the encyclopedia, Eijkman wrongly assumed that the problem arose from a toxic factor in rice.

stations.title: The laboratory: half a gram from a kilo of polishings

paragraphs.text: Funk wrote that before 1911 very little was known about the chemical composition of the protective substance.
He wrote that he began his experiments in the middle of 1911, first in collaboration with Cooper.
According to the encyclopedia, at the Lister Institute Funk prepared a concentrate of rice polishings that cured beriberi in pigeons.
Funk wrote that, by estimate, 20 grams of rice polishings or of their aqueous extract should be sufficient to cure pigeons.
He reported that from a kilogram of rice polishings only half a gram of crystalline substance was obtained.
According to his report, a minute dose of 40 mg of the substance cured a pigeon, sometimes within three hours.

According to the encyclopedia, from the recovery of birds that ate an extract of rice polishings and of yeast, Funk concluded that the essential substance was required in small amounts to maintain health.
According to Funk, the cure with solutions that contained no phosphorus contradicted Schaumann's theory that the disease stems from a phosphorus deficiency.
Funk proposed to call the isolated substance, provisionally, “beri-beri vitamine”.
He proposed speaking of a beriberi vitamin and a scurvy vitamin, meaning a substance that prevents a particular disease.
In a 1912 paper, Funk proposed that there are at least four vitamins.
According to an article in PMC, Funk was the first to suggest the existence of a family of organic substances that are essential for life.
Funk reported that substances capable of curing beriberi were found in milk, yeast, ox brain and lime juice.
According to Funk, only fresh food protects against scurvy, and dried material is completely valueless.
He wrote that he was inclined to think that the scurvy vitamin is different from the beriberi vitamin.
Funk recommended not heating milk more than necessary.
He noted that, according to Mrs. Lane-Claypon, there is no real evidence that infantile scurvy is caused by boiled milk.
According to an article in PMC, Funk's 1912 paper and his book on vitamins attracted the attention of the medical and scientific community.
According to the encyclopedia, the 1912 publication earned Funk public recognition and a Beit Fellowship from the University of London.
According to the encyclopedia, Funk found that diseases such as beriberi, rickets and scurvy could be cured by introducing certain organic compounds into the diet.
According to the same source, in 1936 Funk wrote that a lack of a particular vitamin eventually leads to a particular nutritional disease.
According to the PMC article, the work led to the discovery of 13 vitamins within 35 years.
According to the same article, Funk's Oscodal concentrate was the first vitamin preparation accepted by the American Medical Association as an ethical product.
According to an article in PMC, the US Congress officially marked one hundred years since Funk's discovery of the vitamin.
According to CNBC, the American Nutrition Association inducted Funk into the Nutrition Hall of Fame.
According to Live Science, Google honored Funk with a Doodle on February 23, his 140th birthday.
The Polish Institute of Arts and Sciences of America awards Polish-American scientists a prize named after Funk.
According to an article in PMC, Funk was born in Warsaw, the son of a Polish physician.
According to the encyclopedia, his father, Jacques, was a prominent dermatologist.
Funk came from a Jewish background.
According to the PMC article, the World Wars together with his Polish Jewish ancestry led Funk to a career in the United States and in five European countries.
According to the encyclopedia, he left England in 1915 and was accepted at the Harriman Laboratory in New York.
According to the same source, in 1923, sponsored by the Rockefeller Foundation, Funk returned to Poland and headed the Department of Biochemistry at the State Institute of Hygiene.
According to the encyclopedia, he published more than 140 articles during his lifetime.
According to Time, Funk died of cancer at 83 in Albany, New York.
According to CNBC, citing Google, Funk pursued his studies with passion despite obstacles he faced as a Jewish student in Europe, at a time of rising antisemitism
Funk himself acknowledged in 1912 that the idea that diseases are caused by deficiency was not yet generally accepted.
He wrote that years of experimental work were needed to show that diseases occur which are caused by a deficiency of essential substances in food.
According to Live Science, the idea that diseases are caused by a lack of essential substances, rather than by infection or toxins, was revolutionary.
According to the encyclopedia, Funk never isolated a pure vitamin, but he prepared concentrates that contained several vitamins.

According to the same source, his concentrates were primarily nicotinic acid, which is not effective against beriberi (Elvehjem later showed that it cures pellagra), and they were contaminated with the anti-beriberi vitamin.
According to MDedge, the name “vitamine” remained.
Funk was not the first to isolate thiamine.
According to MDedge, in 1929 Hopkins and Eijkman were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery of vitamins.
According to an article in PMC, vitamins such as C and D are not amines at all, and therefore the word vitamin has no letter e.
According to Live Science, vitamin D, for example, is produced in the body in response to ultraviolet radiation on the skin.
According to the PMC article, Funk's original model aroused scepticism and intense criticism of newer research indicating that vitamins have many actions.
According to the encyclopedia, after Funk's discoveries consumers began to ingest large amounts of vitamins, although small amounts were sufficient.
According to the PMC article, vitamin C has been shown to cure scurvy, but not the common cold.

disagreements.question: In what year was Funk's book on vitamins published?

versions.says: According to an article in PMC, the book Die Vitamine was published two years after the 1912 paper
According to the University of Bristol, Funk published a book called The Vitamines in 1912

disagreements.question: Did Funk isolate the anti-beriberi substance?

versions.says: According to the University of Utah, Funk isolated the active principle from rice polishings and found that it was an amine compound, thiamin.
According to the encyclopedia, Funk never isolated a pure vitamin, but he prepared concentrates that contained several vitamins
According to MDedge, Funk probably isolated nicotinic acid and not the anti-beriberi factor

unknowns.text: The sources here do not say with certainty what the crystalline substance that Funk obtained from rice polishings was

claims.text: לפי המאמר, המודל המקורי של פונק עורר ספקנות וביקורת חריפה כלפי מחקר חדש שהצביע על פעולות מרובות של ויטמינים.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה, בעקבות גילויי פונק צרכנים החלו לבלוע כמויות גדולות של ויטמינים אף שכמויות קטנות הספיקו.
claims.quote: Consumers began to ingest large amounts of vitamins, despite the fact that small amounts were sufficient
